article.info_title: Crawling December: The how and why of Googlebot crawling
article.info_description:
You may have heard that Google Search needs to do a bit of work before a web page can show up in
      Google Search results. One of these steps is called crawling. Crawling for Google Search is done
      by Googlebot, a program running on Google servers that retrieves a URL and handles things like
      network errors, redirects, and other small complications that it might encounter as it works its
      way through the web. But there are a few details that aren't often talked about. Each week this
      month we're going to explore some of those details as they may have a significant effect on how
      your sites are crawled.

article.info_title: Updating our site reputation abuse policy
article.info_description:
Earlier this year, as part of our work to fight spam and deliver a great Search experience,
      we launched a spam policy to combat site reputation abuse.
      We're clarifying our policy language to further target this type of spammy behavior.
      We're making it clear that using third-party content on a site in an attempt to exploit the
      site's ranking signals is a violation of this policy — regardless of whether there is
      first-party involvement or oversight of the content.

article.info_title: #GTMTips: Quickly Duplicate Tags In Google Tag Manager
article.info_description:
There are many reasons why you might want to duplicate your tags (or triggers, or variables, or templates) in Google Tag Manager.
One prime example is server-side tagging, where it’s sensible to first build and validate your tracking setup before migrating fully to a server-side approach.
Alternatively, you might want to collect analytics data to a second property, for example when you want to have a local and a global dataset for site visit data.

You can now use the manual ad content parameter as a condition group when creating a new custom channel. This update enhances your channel analysis by not limiting the channel conditions to only use automatically tagged parameters. You can create a new custom channel group as long as you have Editor or higher permission.
We now help you identify and fix product disapprovals from Google Merchant Center, ensuring your items can appear in Google Shopping results and Shopping ads.
We've made it easier to understand your imported ads cost data in Google Analytics.

You can now use customer match to supplement Analytics audiences exported to your linked Google advertising products like Google Ads, Display & Video 360, or Search Ads 360. If your data includes user-provided data, any audience exported to Google advertising products will match your consented, hashed customer data with Google data. This increases your addressable audience by leveraging first-party data when other identifiers aren't available. It also helps maximize coverage for remarketing efforts, ensuring that your campaigns reach the most relevant audiences.
